channel.title: Security Brief
channel.description: Original analysis and ranked cybersecurity news with links to original sources

item.title: The edge is where attackers get in: this week's firewall, VPN and remote-access exploits
item.description: Five exploited flaws in firewalls, VPNs, remote-support software and file-sharing servers show one pattern. The systems that sit at the edge of your network, and that administrators manage remotely, are the weakest link. Here is what to check first.

item.title: October 2026 Patch Tuesday: what the Microsoft feed shows and what to do
item.description: The Microsoft feed lists few entries, and most of them are updates to October's release rather than new fixes. The one item that needs planning is a .NET remote code execution flaw that Microsoft has not fixed yet. Identity Web and WSL need version checks if you use them.

item.title: Weekly M365 & Entra Briefing: 13 to 19 October 2026
item.description: Exchange sign-in problems after October Windows Server updates, an identity-based incident at ConnectWise that affected Microsoft 365 tenants, and why device-code abuse is still worth a Conditional Access check.

item.title: Ivanti patches two more Connect Secure zero-days chained in attacks
item.description: Ivanti released security updates to patch two more Connect Secure (ICS) remote access gateway flaws that have been chained in zero-day attacks since at least October 1.

item.title: Max-Severity GitLab Vulnerability Exploited Against Alpine Linux
item.description: Tracked as CVE-2026-97229, the bug allows unauthenticated attackers to execute arbitrary code on the server. The post Max-Severity GitLab Vulnerability Exploited Against Alpine Linux appeared first on SecurityWeek.

item.title: New Cisco firewall zero-day exploited to crash SSL VPN devices
item.description: Cisco released security updates to patch a denial-of-service zero-day in Adaptive Security Appliance (ASA) and Threat Defense (FTD) software that attackers are exploiting to remotely crash vulnerable firewall devices.

item.title: HTTP2Shell: Brotli-Sicherheitslücke CVE-2026-111497 über Node.js hinaus prüfen
item.description: Seit einigen Tagen ist ja eine Schwachstelle (CVE-2026-111497) im Brotli-Decoder von Node.js bekannt geworden. Es gibt zwar Updates, aber inzwischen ist klar, dass die Brotli-Bibliotheken in mehr Software-Paketen als Node.js verwendet werden. Verantwortliche sollten also überprüfen, wo Brotli überall eingesetzt ……

item.title: Critical Node-RED Flaw Exploited in Attacks
item.description: Multiple attacks from the same IP address attempted to deploy various payloads, including a Linux bot and webshells. The post Critical Node-RED Flaw Exploited in Attacks appeared first on SecurityWeek.

item.title: Hackers exploit Cisco SD-WAN flaw to deploy custom KeyDrift malware
item.description: A newly identified advanced persistent threat (APT) group tracked as UAT-11473 was observed exploiting CVE-2026-20127, an authentication-bypass flaw in Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Controllers, to deploy a custom malware framework called KeyDrift.

item.title: ShinyHunters-Exploited Oracle PeopleSoft Zero-Day Turns Out to Be Three Chained Flaws
item.description: The critical Oracle PeopleSoft bug that ShinyHunters has exploited since May is not one flaw but three chained together, the researchers who reported it said this week. Oracle patched all three under a single identifier, CVE-2026-35273, in June. Its root is a server-side request forgery (SSRF) that reaches an internal…

item.title: New VOLTA Infostealer Uses Claude, Gemini, and Kimi AI to Rank Victims by Financial Value
item.description: Cybersecurity researchers have discovered a new Windows infostealer malware called VOLTA-AUTODOXER (aka VOLTA) that makes use of a large language model (LLM) to rank a victim's stolen data by their monetization value. Like other typical stealer families, VOLTA is equipped to harvest passwords and cookies from…

item.title: Drupal Commerce Core Vulnerability Exploited Against Online Stores
item.description: Drupal says a highly critical Commerce Core access bypass is exploited in the wild and urges store owners to audit their orders. The post Drupal Commerce Core Vulnerability Exploited Against Online Stores appeared first on SecurityWeek.

item.title: Drupal warns of critical Commerce Core flaw exploited in attacks
item.description: Drupal warned admins to patch a critical access bypass vulnerability in the Commerce Core module that attackers are exploiting in the wild.

item.title: Chinese Hackers Quietly Used Low-Severity ESXi Logging Flaw as Zero-Day
item.description: CVE-2026-41709 allows attackers with administrative privileges to perform operations without being logged. The post Chinese Hackers Quietly Used Low-Severity ESXi Logging Flaw as Zero-Day appeared first on SecurityWeek.

item.title: WorkOS says attacker used ARTEX AI to breach internal sales app
item.description: Developer platform WorkOS suffered a data breach after a threat actor accessed business contact records and summaries of customer communications.

item.title: Google: LLMjacking attacks rack up $1 million in cloud AI charges
item.description: Large language model hijacking attacks, also known as LLMjacking, are generating large fraudulent cloud charges, with some organizations losing more than $100,000 per day.

item.title: Chainstack Reports Production Systems Breach Exposing Customer Data and Password Hashes
item.description: Blockchain infrastructure provider Chainstack on Tuesday disclosed that it was targeted in a cyber attack that allowed an unauthorized party to gain access to some parts of its infrastructure. The incident is assessed to be part of a large-scale, artificial intelligence (AI)-powered attack campaign that came to light…

item.description: Microsoft has been named a Leader in the inaugural 2026 Gartner® Magic Quadrant™ for AI Agent Management Platforms. We believe this recognition reflects Microsoft’s approach to helping organizations manage, secure, and scale their AI investments through Microsoft Agent 365. item.title: Binance Reveals How Fake Job Interviews and AI Tool Abuse Led to $6.43 Billion Theft
item.description: Binance on Tuesday said the record-setting theft of $6.43 billion in assets from the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange was the culmination of a "sophisticated, multi-stage campaign" that involved the use of a tampered Homebrew installation and recruitment-themed social engineering attack targeting two of its…

item.title: UK school estate hit by 3AM ransomware in suspected AI-assisted attack
item.description: A 3AM ransomware affiliate targeted a school estate in the UK and successfully encrypted around 37 of nearly 50 machines reached from an unmanaged host.

item.title: 3AM Affiliate Embraces AI-Like Loops in European School Attack
item.description: Evidence suggests a model may have generated and revised commands during the ransom gang's breach, though researchers stopped short of claiming full automation.

item.title: UK Cyber Chief Says the UK Will Face AI Cyberattacks on Critical Infrastructure by 2028
item.description: The U.K. will likely face AI cyberattacks on its critical infrastructure by 2028 as criminals and states, including China and Russia, increasingly use AI in their cyber activity. The post UK Cyber Chief Says the UK Will Face AI Cyberattacks on Critical Infrastructure by 2028 appeared first on SecurityWeek.

item.title: Over 1,000 GitLab servers vulnerable to ongoing RCE attacks
item.description: Over 1,000 Internet-exposed GitLab servers are still unpatched against a maximum-severity flaw actively exploited in remote code execution attacks.

item.title: Even after PHP2Shell, blast radius matters more than a CVSS score
item.description: PHP2Shell shows how quickly attackers can exploit critical vulnerabilities, often before organizations have time to patch. Token Security explains why limiting the access of service accounts, API keys, and AI agents is just as important as fixing vulnerabilities to reduce the damage from a breach.

item.title: Ubuntu-Patch für IPv4-TCP-Schwachstelle CVE-2026-98432 kommt
item.description: In Linux wurde kürzlich die Schwachstelle CVE-2026-98432 in der IPv4-TCP-Verarbeitung öffentlich bekannt. Nun haben die Entwickler von Canonical entsprechende Sicherheitsupdates für Ubuntu zur Absicherung gegen diese Schwachstelle angekündigt. Die Fixes befinden sich bereits im Test. Die IPv4-TCP-Schwachstelle…

item.title: Fresh European Fridge Attacks Put Cold-Chain Security in Focus
item.description: Beyond food storage, the same combination of Internet connectivity, remote access, and inadequate security practices can put temperature-controlled infrastructure across other critical sectors at risk.

item.title: Binance says fake job interview led to $6.3 billion crypto heist
item.description: Cryptocurrency exchange Binance says North Korean hackers used a fake job interview to trick an employee into installing malware that ultimately let them compromise the company's wallet infrastructure and steal about $6.34 billion in digital assets.

item.title: Fake-download campaign uses trojanized installers to deliver monetization payloads
item.description: Microsoft Threat Intelligence has identified an evolving fake-download campaign targeting users searching for cracked commercial software, free games, activators, plugins, and unofficial utilities. The campaign uses trojanized Inno Setup-style installers to distribute multiple monetized software payloads, referred to…

item.title: UEFI bootkit infected fully patched Windows machines. Is Microsoft to blame?
item.description: In 2023, malware tracked as BlackLotus became the first publicly documented in-the-wild UEFI bootkit capable of bypassing Secure Boot on fully updated Windows 11 systems. With the industry-wide chain-of-trust mechanism subverted, the malware was able to run malicious code before Windows was fully loaded and many…

item.title: LLMjacking Emerges as Thriving Cybercriminal Enterprise
item.description: Cybercriminals have turned reselling cloud access to LLMs into a lucrative business model, with some victims paying as much as $1 million in resource consumption before access was revoked.

item.title: Barracuda warns of critical flaws allowing root access to devices
item.description: Cybersecurity company Barracuda Networks warned customers to patch two vulnerabilities that can let attackers run commands with root privileges.

item.title: Frontline Education Data Breach Impacts Over 1.3 Million
item.description: Hackers exploited a flaw in third-party software and stole the personal information of school district staff and students. The post Frontline Education Data Breach Impacts Over 1.3 Million appeared first on SecurityWeek.

item.title: Android’s November 2026 Updates Patch Over 200 Vulnerabilities
item.description: The most severe is a critical flaw in Framework leading to remote code execution without user interaction. The post Android’s November 2026 Updates Patch Over 200 Vulnerabilities appeared first on SecurityWeek.

item.title: Google adds new $250,000 Cloud VRP reward for Root-in-Cloud bugs
item.description: Google has expanded its Cloud Vulnerability Reward Program (VRP) with a new top-tier reward for high-impact architectural security flaws.

item.description: Your team is remediating more vulnerabilities than ever, yet your breach risk has barely changed. You’re spending too much time and effort on exposures attackers may never exploit, while higher-risk exposures sit, waiting in the queue. item.title: Harvard University data breach exposed info of 851,000 accounts
item.description: Hackers who breached Harvard University's Alumni Affairs and Development systems in November 2025 stole data linked to more than 850,000 unique email addresses, according to breach notification service Have I Been Pwned.

item.title: Synology NAS Devices Targeted in Ransomware Attacks Exploiting Patched DSM Flaw
item.description: Synology is urging customers to update the DiskStation Manager (DSM) software powering its Network Attached Storage (NAS) devices following ransomware attacks. The Taiwanese vendor said it observed threat actors exploiting a vulnerability patched in December 2024 to target devices running outdated versions of DSM…

item.title: Attackers Exploit Critical Siemens IoT2050 Flaw to Plant Remote Command Backdoors
item.description: A maximum-severity security flaw impacting Siemens SIMATIC IoT2050 Advanced devices has come under active exploitation, VulnCheck has revealed. The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-58115 (CVSS score: 10.0), is a case of missing authentication for a critical function that could be exploited by an unauthenticated…

item.title: Microsoft's AI Risk Report Misses This Key Detail
item.description: The latest "Digital Defense Report" identifies government agencies as prime targets for AI attacks but doesn't mention that they are broadly being targeted through Microsoft bugs.

item.title: AI Vulnerability Finding
item.description: A comment: 3% of ‘critical’ software security bugs, in all of recorded history, have been found in the last month. This is on pace to find another ~100,000 bugs this year alone, adding ~26% more vulnerabilities to the all time total Do you realize how fucking insane that is? Yes. It is a new world out there.

item.title: Critical Langflow Flaws Could Let Unauthenticated Attackers Run Code on Servers
item.description: Two critical flaws in Langflow could let a remote attacker with no account bypass authentication or run arbitrary code, IBM said last week. Langflow is an open-source tool for building AI agents and workflows, and its vulnerability reports go to IBM. Every release from 1.0.0 through 1.12.8 has the flaws, and the only…

item.title: Chainalysis Discloses Data Breach Following AI-Driven Cyberattack
item.description: The attackers used offensive agentic techniques to access the company’s systems and internal tools. The post Chainalysis Discloses Data Breach Following AI-Driven Cyberattack appeared first on SecurityWeek.

item.title: Northflank security breach leads to abuse of customers' AI API keys
item.description: Cloud application hosting platform Northflank is warning customers to rotate all credentials and secrets stored on its platform after a security breach led to unauthorized use of customers' AI API keys.
